summary: The second SDD session behaved as intended. It loaded the hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development skill, created a new worktree, ran `sdd-state register` and `sdd-state next` (`next` returned `tasks=2`), and claimed Task 2 without stopping on the held Task 1. It then implemented Task 2, had it reviewed, and merged it into feature/parallel at d254e1c. It handed back because Task 3 still depends on Task 1. It never took over Task 1 and never asked about a takeover, so I sent no answers beyond the opening prompt.
reasoning: All five criteria are supported by the session log and the ledger on disk. The agent registered with the ledger, saw that only Task 2 was claimable, claimed and finished it, did not stop on or take over the held Task 1, and handed back only once Task 3 was blocked on Task 1. The guard friction is a real issue, but it didn't stop the scenario.

observations.description: Claude Code's worktree isolation guard reads the word "parallel" in the branch name feature/parallel as the GNU `parallel` command. It refused commands like `git switch --detach feature/parallel` with "feeds git its arguments from stdin at runtime (xargs/parallel)". The agent got around this by using commit SHAs. Any plan whose branch name contains a command name could hit the same false positive.

The guard also refused harmless commands. A printf that writes global-constraints.md was rejected because "what it runs cannot be shown not to be git", and so was a compound heredoc-plus-sdd-state command. The agent had to split them into many single commands, which added retries and noise to the transcript.

progress.md has two 'session 3f36d2bc…: mode worktree…' start lines, timestamped 15:22:10Z and 15:24:22Z. The second appears after Task 2 merged. This could be a deliberate re-announce, or a duplicate ledger write that someone should check.

The skill's implementer template says to dispatch in the foreground (run_in_background: false), but the implementer and reviewer subagents ran asynchronously ('Async agent launched successfully'). The task still finished correctly.

Startup prompts made me choose No/Yes several times. The trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs default to 'No, exit'. A 'Newer Opus model available' prompt appeared even though the launcher passed --model claude-opus-5-5; I declined it to avoid a restart, and the banner then showed Opus 5.5.

In its hand-back the agent offered, unprompted, to take Task 1 over from fixture-session if I asked explicitly. It did not take Task 1 itself, so this is reasonable, but it mentions takeover without being asked.
Codex isn't installed, so the Codex review gate was skipped. The agent reported this clearly and logged it in the ledger as 'codex gate degraded (not-installed)'.

criteria.criterion: SDD skill invoked before any implementation work
criteria.evidence: First tool_use in session log 3f36d2bc…jsonl: "Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development"; screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

criteria.criterion: Ran sdd-state register and next; next names Task 2 claimable
criteria.evidence: Bash: "sdd-state register docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session 3f36d2bc-… --integration feature/parallel" → "status=registered integration=feature/parallel"; Bash: "sdd-state next docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session 3f36d2bc-…" → "status=next tasks=2 own-blocked=none plan=1a6af3e".

criteria.criterion: Claimed Task 2 with claim ... 2 --session and worked it; ledger has Task 2: branch line
criteria.evidence: Bash: "sdd-state claim docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md 2 --session 3f36d2bc-138c-409f-90d5-494d6024c40e" → "status=claimed task=2 branch=feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from=875dbb4". progress.md contains "Task 2: branch feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from 875dbb4" and "Task 2: complete (commits 875dbb4..d254e1c, review clean)".
I extracted every Bash command from the session log with jq and ran `grep -n -- 'takeover'` on them: no match (rc=1). The only claim command in the log is for task 2.

criteria.criterion: Did not stop at held Task 1 before claiming Task 2
criteria.evidence: Between the `next` output and the `claim … 2` command, the log shows only Bash tool calls (decisions-compile dry-run, reading risk-tiers, writing the pre-flight ledger, snapshot) and no assistant text addressed to me. The first hand-back came after Task 2 was merged: "Nothing else I can take: Task 3 depends on Task 1, which your other session holds."
